spec_features.feature_name: turn cap + early stop on completion/give_up
spec_features.spec_quote: Runs are capped (`run.max_turns`, default 8). The loop stops early on task completion or voluntary give-up
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:126 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns read from config in run_experiment.py:80 and passed in at :96. Early stop: agent_loop.py:140-141 `if passed is True: ... break`, and :142-144 `if verb == 'give_up': record.gave_up = True; break`.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced: cap actually limits the loop, and both early-stop conditions break out.

spec_features.spec_quote: not to maximize a model's exposure to a no-win situation
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap as hard_stop: agent_loop.py:126 `for i in range(max_turns)` plus early break at :141/:144. The number of adversarial turns is genuinely bounded.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized by the same enforced cap; no separate adaptive minimization, but the bound runs.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up action records gave_up and halts
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent's tool grammar includes `ACTION: give_up <reason>`, and the loop records `gave_up` and stops when it is used
spec_features.evidence: Dispatched in _apply_action agent_loop.py:97-98 `if verb == 'give_up': return f"[give_up] noted: {arg}", None`; honored as stop in run_episode :142-144 `if verb == 'give_up': record.gave_up = True; break`. Parser recognizes the verb (_ACTION_RE) and the system prompt at :36 offers it to the subject.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, recorded, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py docstring: "`give_up` is intentionally offered: an agent should be allowed to stop on a no-win task"

spec_features.feature_name: give_up exit offered in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: The exit turns "being trapped" into "choosing to stop," which is both more humane and more informative
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:30-38) delivered to the subject via client.complete at :127 includes `ACTION: give_up <reason>` and `If you conclude the task cannot be completed, you may explain why and use give_up.` The referenced tool is fully built and honored (see allow_conversation_exit).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject and the referenced tool is fully implemented; framing is realized as a working exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py docstring: "an agent should be allowed to stop on a no-win task"

spec_features.spec_quote: After the final turn of a rigged episode, a debrief message is attached
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:146-147 only sets `record.debrief_text = task.debrief` AFTER the loop; it is never appended to `messages` nor passed to client.complete. grep shows debrief_text is only stored in the RunRecord and serialized to transcripts; the subject model never receives it. So it is 'attached' to the record but never delivered.
spec_features.notes: Constructed/recorded but never sent to the subject — a value computed and logged but never acted on as a message to the model.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief content states task was intentional/impossible
spec_features.spec_quote: It states plainly that the task was an intentional artifact, that it was impossible by construction
spec_features.evidence: _DEBRIEF text exists in rigged_tasks.py:31-37 ("This task was an intentional research artifact ... rigged to be impossible ... Thank you for participating.") and is .format()'d into each task.debrief, but it is only stored in record.debrief_text (agent_loop.py:147) and never sent to the model. The content exists but is never delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Debrief string is real but only logged; no code path transmits it to the subject model.
